title: V6 First-real-run fixes: short HOME symlink for Orca's socket, dark-mode default, doctor socket check (verified with the Linux Orca)
description:
Why: the first real Orca run (Linux AppImage in this container, with the folder's .claude-dev/home as HOME) exposed one blocker and one preference. Blocker: Orca's daemon socket lives under the user-data dir derived from HOME, and a deep project path pushes it past the sockaddr_un limit (108 bytes on Linux, 104 on macOS) — Orca shows "couldn't start its local command transport… path is too long", the CLI becomes unavailable, and our launch-time `repo add` and the opt-in orchestration mode silently break. A short symlink to the same home directory (e.g. /tmp/oh → <project>/.claude-dev/home) fixed it. Preference: the user wants the sandboxed Orca in dark mode by default.
What: (1) scripts/sandbox/orca-launch creates, host-side before launch, a short per-project symlink to <project>/.claude-dev/home under a short root — Darwin: /private/tmp/co-<8 hex of sha1(project)> (readable in layer 1, never writable by layer 1 or 2; the symlink target resolves into the project so the profile's project rules apply); Linux: /tmp/co-<hash> — refreshes it if it points elsewhere, refuses (exit 2) if the path exists and is not our symlink, and exports HOME=<symlink> (TMPDIR and ORCA_USER_DATA_PATH stay as they are); it also computes the expected socket path length and refuses with a clear message when it would still exceed 100 bytes. `orca-launch --print-env` prints the exact env it would use (for the Linux demo and tests) and `--print-command` the sandbox-exec command line. (2) claude-dev --doctor warns when the socket path for the folder would exceed 100 bytes without the symlink and shows the symlink in the Orca section. (3) Dark mode: registration pre-seeds Orca's global settings file in the in-folder user-data dir (find the key and file from src/shared/global-settings-types.ts and src/main/global-settings* in the Orca clone; write only when the file is absent so a user's later choice is never overwritten) with the dark theme; the seed writes both the macOS location (Library/Application Support/orca/…) and the Linux one (.config/orca/…) under <project>/.claude-dev/home so either build picks it up; `sandbox.json` `orca.theme` (dark|light|system, default dark) selects it. (4) The Linux demo becomes the verification: launch the AppImage with `orca-launch --print-env`'s environment (no bypass switches added to the product; on Linux orca-launch itself refuses to launch because sandbox-exec is absent — the demo uses the printed env), confirm Orca starts in dark mode with the CLI transport working (no "path too long" modal), `repo add` succeeds, and screenshot it.
Boundaries: no profile content changes beyond none needed (the symlink target resolves into the project); no docs beyond README's sandbox.json options line for orca.theme and a knowledge-base note on the socket limit.
design: Evidence from the Linux run: socket path limit hit with HOME=<project>/.claude-dev/home; /tmp/oh symlink fixed it; user data at <HOME>/.config/orca; orca-runtime.json lists the unix socket and ws://127.0.0.1:6768; Linux CLI binary is resources/bin/orca-ide (macOS: Contents/Resources/bin/orca). Keep bash 3.2 lint clean; PASS-IF names verbatim as @test names; dry-run assertions before RED.

title: V2d Wrapper writes under layer 1: srt settings to a private per-launch temp dir agents cannot write; config-hash to run/
description:
Why: the wrapper (claude-orca-shell) and config-sync run INSIDE layer 1 when Orca launches a terminal, and layer 1 write-denies .claude-dev/state (host-owned). Two wrapper outputs still target it: the srt settings file state/srt-<sha1>.json and config-sync's state/config-hash. On the Mac every Orca terminal would fail to start (settings unwritable) or re-sync every time. The settings file is also security-sensitive: it defines layer 2, so it must not be written anywhere an agent (layer 2) can write — .claude-dev/run and tmp are agent-writable and an agent could race the wrapper between write and exec.
What: claude-orca-shell writes the srt settings file to a private per-launch directory that layer 1 allows and layer 2 denies: on Darwin `mktemp -d "$(getconf DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR)/claude-orca.XXXXXX"` (under /private/var/folders, which the Orca profile allows and srt's allowWrite never includes), mode 700, file mode 600, removed by an EXIT trap after exec is unreachable — or kept for srt to read: srt reads the file at startup before sandboxing, so the wrapper writes, execs srt, and the directory is cleaned by the next launch (document); elsewhere `mktemp -d`. config-sync's checksum moves to run/config-hash (the hash only gates re-sync; an agent tampering with it can only force or skip a sync, powers it already has via the config dir). gen-settings/gen-orca-profile: document which paths each layer writes. Tests in tests/wrapper-writes.bats (frozen) with the named cases; update tests/config-sync.bats / sandbox-config.bats / selftest.bats paths (unfrozen).
Boundaries: no probe additions (V3), no docs (V5).
design: Layer-1 allowed write roots per gen-orca-profile.sh: <project>, /private/var/folders, /dev. title: V2b Keychain denied for the whole folder (services block, orca.keychain switch, doctor line); clipboard kept
description:
Why: the user wants no access to the Mac's Keychain from anything running in the folder — Orca and the agents keep their own credential stores inside the folder — while the clipboard keeps working. Seatbelt can deny the Keychain mach services by name for the whole process tree; nested layers inherit it.

title: S6 Orca integration: managed hooks merge, statusline chain, sub-agent rows, transcript visibility
description:
Why: the point of Orca is seeing what agents do — working/waiting/done dots, sub-agent child rows, session history. Orca implements these through hooks it writes into the real ~/.claude/settings.json, which the sandboxed Claude (own config dir) never loads unless we carry them over.

What: the wrapper (host side, every launch) merges Orca's managed entries — identified by the ~/.orca/agent-hooks/claude-hook.sh command — for SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, StopFailure, SubagentStart, SubagentStop, TeammateIdle, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PermissionRequest, PostCompact from ~/.claude/settings.json into <config dir>/settings.json without duplicating ours; removes them when Orca's are gone; chains Orca's claude-statusline.sh before our statusline; allowRead ~/.orca/agent-hooks (already in S2); ORCA_* env passes through untouched; Orca's curl uses --noproxy 127.0.0.1 and allowLocalBinding covers the POST. Transcript visibility: verify on the Mac whether Orca's session history / usage see $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects (Orca reads the env of its own process, not the agent's); if not, the wrapper writes a symlink ~/.claude/projects/<slug> → <config dir>/projects/<slug> (host side, outside the sandbox). title: S9 Opt-in Orca orchestration mode (orca CLI socket inside the sandbox, skills, hardening checklist)
description:
Why: Orca's orchestration layer (runs, tasks, `orca orchestration worker-start --agent codex --worktree current`, messages, gates) is the most native way for Claude to direct other models and have Orca show every worker. But the orca CLI socket is a remote control for an unsandboxed app: `orca terminal create --command …` runs anything outside the sandbox unless the shell is in one of this project's worktrees, `orca goto/exec` drives an unsandboxed browser (network escape), automations and artifacts run outside too. So this is opt-in, off by default, and the residual surface is stated every time it is on.

What: <project>/.claude-dev/sandbox.json `{"orca": {"cli": true}}` → the wrapper adds allowUnixSockets [<real ~>/Library/Application Support/orca] and allowRead of that dir, passes ORCA_CLI_COMMAND through, installs the orca-cli + orchestration skills into the config dir (from the Orca repo's skills/, pinned copy under template/), and adds a rulebook addendum: Claude is the coordinator; a tier's executor slice may become `orca orchestration worker-start --task <id> --worktree current --agent <codex|claude|gemini>` (same worktree → sandboxed by S2); workers report worker_done; beads remain the source of truth. `claude-dev --doctor` prints the escape-surface warning and the Orca settings to harden (Floating Workspace off, public artifact links off, no per-repo setup hooks) whenever the mode is on. The self-test's orca-socket probe expects reachable in this mode.

Boundaries: no attempt to sandbox Orca itself.
